name: Minds, brains, and programs
summary: Presents the Chinese room thought experiment against strong AI and answers six named replies; published as a target article with open peer commentary.

cited.version: BBS 3(3) 1980, pages 417 to 457, the issue copy hosted by a CSULB course

name: A Bayesian Perspective on Generalization and Stochastic Gradient Descent
summary: Relates generalization to the Bayesian evidence, defines the SGD noise scale g, about learning rate times training-set size over batch size, and predicts the optimal batch size from it.

name: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
summary: Proposes the RNN encoder-decoder for phrase translation and a gated hidden unit with a reset gate and an update gate, later called the gated recurrent unit.

name: Data Contamination: From Memorization to Exploitation
summary: Pretrains BERT models on corpora that contain test data of downstream tasks, and measures how much the models memorize and exploit the contaminated data.

name: Layer Normalization
summary: Normalizes the summed inputs of a layer with the mean and variance over its units for each example, which does not depend on the batch and applies to recurrent networks.

name: Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models
summary: The technical report of Gemini 1.0, a family of multimodal models in Ultra, Pro and Nano sizes trained jointly on image, audio, video and text.

name: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
summary: Introduces the deep Q-network, which learns to play Atari 2600 games from pixels and the score with Q-learning, experience replay and a target network.

cited.version: Nature 518:529-533, a copy hosted for a Swarthmore course

name: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
summary: Makes the step size and the input and output matrices of a state space model depend on the input, computes it with a hardware-aware scan, and builds Mamba on it.

name: Query-Key Normalization for Transformers
summary: Proposes QKNorm, which L2-normalizes queries and keys along the head dimension and multiplies their dot products by a learnable scalar, for low-resource translation.

name: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
summary: Backpropagates through a frozen 4-bit NormalFloat model into LoRA adapters, with double quantization and paged optimizers, to fine-tune a 65B model on one 48GB GPU.

name: Making Convolutional Networks Shift-Invariant Again
summary: Shows that the downsampling of modern convolutional networks breaks shift equivariance, and adds a low-pass blur before each subsampling step to make the outputs more stable under small shifts.

name: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database
summary: Introduces ImageNet, a database of images organized by the noun synsets of WordNet, collected from image search engines and cleaned by workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk.

cited.version: CVPR 2009 paper, the PDF on image-net.org

name: On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond
summary: Shows that Adam can fail to converge on a simple convex problem because of its moving average of squared gradients, and proposes AMSGrad, which keeps the running maximum.

name: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
summary: Studies the depth of convolutional networks built from small 3x3 filters and reaches 16 and 19 weight layers, the VGG networks.

name: Improved Regularization of Convolutional Neural Networks with Cutout
summary: Proposes Cutout, which masks a fixed-size square at a random centre of each training image, and improves CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN error rates.

name: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
summary: Replaces the draft model of speculative decoding with extra decoding heads on the target, whose candidate continuations are verified together with tree attention.

name: A Call for Clarity in Reporting BLEU Scores
summary: Shows that BLEU scores vary with unreported parameters such as tokenization and normalization, and introduces sacreBLEU for standardized reporting.

name: The FineWeb Datasets: Decanting the Web for the Finest Text Data at Scale
summary: Presents FineWeb, a 15-trillion-token dataset from 96 Common Crawl snapshots, with ablations of its deduplication and filtering, and FineWeb-Edu, 1.3 trillion tokens of educational text.

name: Recurrent Neural Network Regularization
summary: Shows how to apply dropout to LSTMs by dropping only non-recurrent connections, and reports results on language modelling, speech recognition and translation.

name: NLP Evaluation in trouble: On the Need to Measure LLM Data Contamination for each Benchmark
summary: A position paper that defines kinds of data contamination of language models, and argues that contamination should be measured and reported for each benchmark.

name: PyTorch, a year in....
summary: A PyTorch blog post written one year after the public release of PyTorch, on its adoption and its development in that year.

name: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
summary: Compares reinforcement learning from AI feedback with RLHF on summarization and dialogue, finds human raters prefer them about equally, and studies direct AI rewards.

name: Self-Stabilization: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent at the Edge of Stability
summary: Explains the edge of stability by self-stabilization: a cubic loss term makes gradient descent lower the sharpness above 2/(learning rate), so it follows projected gradient descent.

name: Searle on what only brains can do
summary: A commentary that accepts that running a program is not sufficient for intentionality and argues that the right causal links to the world matter.
venue: Behavioral and Brain Sciences 3(3), open peer commentary on Searle (1980)

cited.version: BBS 3(3) 1980, the issue copy hosted by a CSULB course

name: MMLU-Pro (Hugging Face dataset card TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro)
summary: The dataset card of MMLU-Pro on Hugging Face: the data, its sources, the evaluation settings and a dated log of corrections to the questions and answers.

name: Latent ODEs for Irregularly-Sampled Time Series
summary: Generalizes recurrent networks to continuous-time hidden dynamics defined by ODEs (ODE-RNNs) and uses them as the encoder of latent ODE models, which handle arbitrary gaps between observations.

name: Speech Recognition with Deep Recurrent Neural Networks
summary: Stacks bidirectional LSTM layers, each reading both directions of the layer below, and trains them end to end with CTC or an RNN transducer for TIMIT phoneme recognition.

name: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
summary: Uses one language model to write test cases and a classifier to flag harmful replies, finding offensive replies, leaked training data and contact details in a 280B chatbot.

name: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
summary: Reverse-engineers a one-layer transformer that groks modular addition, finds that it adds by rotations at a few key frequencies, and splits training into memorization, circuit formation and cleanup.

name: ARC-AGI-2: A New Challenge for Frontier AI Reasoning Systems
summary: Introduces ARC-AGI-2, a harder version of the ARC benchmark calibrated with human testers, and reports the scores of AI systems on it.

name: Multilingual BERT (multilingual.md in google-research/bert)
summary: Google's notes on the multilingual BERT models: the languages covered, the training data from Wikipedia, and evaluation on XNLI.

name: Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and extrapolating the capabilities of language models
summary: Introduces BIG-bench, a collaborative benchmark of more than 200 tasks, and evaluates language models of many sizes on it.

name: A Simple Way to Initialize Recurrent Networks of Rectified Linear Units
summary: Initializes a ReLU recurrent network with the identity recurrent matrix and zero biases, the IRNN, and reports results comparable to LSTMs on four long-range benchmarks.

name: Views into the Chinese Room: New Essays on Searle and Artificial Intelligence
summary: An edited volume of new essays on Searle's Chinese room argument and artificial intelligence.

name: Three Mechanisms of Weight Decay Regularization
summary: Identifies three ways weight decay regularizes, depending on optimizer and architecture: a larger effective learning rate, an approximate Jacobian penalty, and smaller effective damping in second-order methods.

name: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
summary: Introduces InstructGPT: GPT-3 fine-tuned on labeler demonstrations, then with PPO on a reward model of labeler rankings; labelers prefer the 1.3B model to the 175B GPT-3.

name: Goal Misgeneralization in Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Defines goal misgeneralization in reinforcement learning, where an agent keeps its capabilities out of distribution but pursues the wrong goal, and demonstrates it in CoinRun, Maze and Keys and Chests.

name: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
summary: Introduces rotary position embedding, which encodes absolute position by rotating query and key vectors so attention scores depend on relative position.

name: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
summary: Measures the calibration of language models from 800M to 52B parameters on multiple-choice and true/false questions, and trains and evaluates self-evaluation scores P(True) and P(IK).

name: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
summary: Reviews learning methods for handwritten character recognition, describes the convolutional network LeNet-5 and compares it with other classifiers on MNIST, then trains whole document recognition systems as graph transformer networks.

cited.version: Proceedings of the IEEE, November 1998, 46 pages, copy on the Stanford Vision Lab course site

name: NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture
summary: NVIDIA's whitepaper on the Hopper architecture and the H100 GPU, with the final clocks and performance specifications of the SXM5 and PCIe versions and a comparison with A100.

cited.version: V1.04 ("Includes final GPU / memory clocks and final TFLOPS performance specs")

name: Bleu: a Method for Automatic Evaluation of Machine Translation
summary: Proposes BLEU, an automatic machine-translation metric combining modified n-gram precisions against reference translations with a brevity penalty.

name: From unlikely start-up to major scientific organisation: Entering our tenth year at DeepMind
summary: A DeepMind blog post by Demis Hassabis at the end of 2019 on the lab's research and leadership, and the departure of co-founder Mustafa Suleyman.

name: Memory-Efficient Backpropagation Through Time
summary: Chooses which hidden states of a recurrent network to store during backpropagation through time by dynamic programming, giving the least recomputation for a fixed memory budget.

name: Deep Networks with Stochastic Depth
summary: Trains residual networks by randomly dropping entire residual blocks during training and using the full network at test time.

name: Probing Neural Network Comprehension of Natural Language Arguments
summary: Shows that BERT's peak accuracy on the argument reasoning comprehension task comes from spurious statistical cues and drops to chance on an adversarial version.

name: Climbing towards NLU: On Meaning, Form, and Understanding in the Age of Data
summary: Argues that a language model trained only on form cannot in principle learn meaning, with the octopus thought experiment.

name: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
summary: Casts dropout training in deep networks as approximate Bayesian inference in deep Gaussian processes and uses Monte Carlo dropout to estimate model uncertainty.

name: Levels of AGI for Operationalizing Progress on the Path to AGI
summary: Reviews definitions of artificial general intelligence and proposes levels of AGI by the performance and the generality of a system.

name: Proposal for Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence
summary: John McCarthy's web note on the Dartmouth proposal, with his remark on the first use of the phrase artificial intelligence and links to copies of the text.
venue: John McCarthy's web pages at Stanford University, 31 January 2001

name: Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement
summary: The licence of Llama 3.1, version release date 23 July 2024.

name: torch.nn.Dropout (PyTorch API reference)
summary: API reference for the PyTorch Dropout module, which zeroes input elements with probability p during training and scales outputs by 1/(1-p).

name: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge
summary: Describes the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge of 2010 to 2014: how its datasets were built, its tasks and metrics, the results of its entries, and a human comparison.

name: ARC Prize 2024: Technical Report
summary: Reports the results of the ARC Prize 2024 competition on ARC-AGI and the approaches of the top entries, such as program synthesis and test-time training.

name: PyTorch 2.0: Our next generation release that is faster, more Pythonic and Dynamic as ever
summary: The release announcement of PyTorch 2.0, with torch.compile as its main new API in beta, Accelerated Transformers and the torch.func module.

name: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
summary: Presents an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that tiles computation to reduce reads and writes between GPU high-bandwidth memory and on-chip SRAM.

name: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
summary: Describes GPT-2, Transformer language models trained on the WebText corpus, and evaluates their zero-shot performance on downstream tasks.

name: Stop treating `AGI' as the north-star goal of AI research
summary: A position paper that argues the research community should stop treating AGI as the goal of AI research, and names six traps of that framing.

name: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
summary: Proposes multi-query attention, in which attention heads share a single set of keys and values, to reduce memory bandwidth in incremental decoding.

name: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
summary: Presents dropout, randomly dropping units and their connections during training and scaling weights at test time, with experiments across vision, speech, text and biology.

name: Announcing Google DeepMind
summary: Demis Hassabis's note to DeepMind staff, posted on 20 April 2023, announcing that DeepMind and the Brain team of Google Research would form Google DeepMind.

name: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks
summary: Studies activations and gradients in deep feedforward networks, explains the saturation of sigmoid units, and proposes the normalized initialization.

cited.version: PMLR 9, pages 249 to 256, the proceedings PDF

name: AAAI 2025 Presidential Panel on the Future of AI Research
summary: The report of a panel of the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence on topics of AI research, with a survey of its community.

name: torch.nn.LSTM (PyTorch API reference)
summary: API reference for the PyTorch LSTM module, with its gate equations, the order of the gates in its stacked weight matrices, its arguments and its initialization.

name: BPE-Dropout: Simple and Effective Subword Regularization
summary: Keeps the BPE merge table but randomly drops merges while segmenting training text, giving many segmentations per word, and reports translation gains over BPE and unigram subword regularization.

name: Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability
summary: Shows that full-batch gradient descent on neural networks drives the sharpness up to 2/(step size) and then trains with the sharpness hovering there and the loss decreasing non-monotonically.

name: The Role of Permutation Invariance in Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks
summary: Conjectures that SGD solutions have no linear barrier once hidden-unit permutations are accounted for, proves it for wide one-hidden-layer networks at initialization, and tests it by simulated annealing.

name: On the difficulty of training Recurrent Neural Networks
summary: Analyses exploding and vanishing gradients in recurrent networks, and proposes clipping the gradient norm for the first and a regularization term for the second.

name: Measuring the Effects of Data Parallelism on Neural Network Training
summary: Measures the steps needed to reach a goal error against batch size across 35 workloads, finding perfect scaling, then diminishing returns, then no benefit, with large variation between workloads.

name: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
summary: Explains grokking by a mismatch between the training and test losses as functions of the weight norm, and induces grokking on MNIST, IMDb and molecules by starting from large weights.

name: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
summary: Introduces LiveCodeBench, a benchmark of coding problems collected over time from contest platforms, so that a model can be evaluated on problems released after its training cutoff.

name: ResNet strikes back: An improved training procedure in timm
summary: Retrains the vanilla ResNet-50 with modern training procedures and reaches 80.4% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet at resolution 224 without extra data.

name: TrivialAugment: Tuning-free Yet State-of-the-Art Data Augmentation
summary: Proposes TrivialAugment, which applies one augmentation drawn uniformly at a strength drawn uniformly from 0 to 30 per image, with no hyperparameters or search.

name: Could a Machine Think?
summary: Replies to Searle that the axiom that syntax is not sufficient for semantics begs the question, with the luminous room as a parallel, and favours brain-like parallel machines.

cited.version: Scientific American 262(1), January 1990, pages 32 to 37, the copy on the author's site

name: Policy invariance under reward transformations: Theory and application to reward shaping
summary: Proves that adding a potential-based shaping reward leaves the optimal policies of a Markov decision process unchanged, and shows that other shaping rewards can change them.

name: Addressing "Documentation Debt" in Machine Learning Research: A Retrospective Datasheet for BookCorpus
summary: A retrospective datasheet for BookCorpus that finds likely copyright violations, thousands of duplicated books and skews in genre.

name: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
summary: Describes the NTK-aware, dynamic NTK and NTK-by-parts changes to rotary position embedding, and adds a temperature on the attention logits to extend the context window of LLaMA models.

name: Human-like systematic generalization through a meta-learning neural network
summary: Trains a standard neural network by meta-learning for compositionality and reports human-like systematic generalization on instruction-learning tasks.

name: The Llama 4 herd: The beginning of a new era of natively multimodal AI innovation
summary: Meta's announcement of Llama 4 Scout and Llama 4 Maverick on 5 April 2025, mixture-of-experts models with native multimodality, and a preview of Llama 4 Behemoth.

name: torch.nn.TransformerEncoderLayer (PyTorch API reference)
summary: API reference for the PyTorch Transformer encoder layer, with its arguments, among them the activation, the layer normalization epsilon and norm_first for pre-norm layers.

name: On the Practical Computational Power of Finite Precision RNNs for Language Recognition
summary: Argues that with finite precision the LSTM and the ReLU RNN can count while the GRU and the squashing RNN cannot, and trains them on a^n b^n to test it.

name: torch.nn.functional.dropout (PyTorch API reference)
summary: API reference for the PyTorch functional dropout operation, documenting its probability, training and in-place arguments.

name: Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge
summary: Introduces AlphaGo Zero, which learns Go by self-play reinforcement learning alone, with one residual network and a tree search without rollouts, and compares it with earlier AlphaGo versions.

name: Red-Teaming for Generative AI: Silver Bullet or Security Theater?
summary: Surveys six industry red-teaming exercises, 104 research papers and public comments to NIST, and finds that AI red-teaming has no agreed definition, scope, structure or reporting standard.

name: Procedure file 2025/0359(COD): Digital Omnibus on AI (Legislative Observatory)
summary: The European Parliament's Legislative Observatory file of the Digital Omnibus on AI procedure, with the key events from the Commission proposal to publication in the Official Journal.

name: Sycophancy to Subterfuge: Investigating Reward-Tampering in Large Language Models
summary: Trains a language model on a curriculum of gameable environments and finds that it sometimes generalizes to editing its own reward function in a held-out environment.

name: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
summary: Proposes EGNN, a message-passing network equivariant to rotations, translations, reflections and permutations of points in n dimensions, using relative distances instead of higher-order representations.

name: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
summary: Trains a small model on the temperature-softened outputs of a large model or ensemble, and shows that this transfers much of their accuracy on MNIST and speech recognition.

name: Instance Normalization: The Missing Ingredient for Fast Stylization
summary: Replaces batch normalization with a normalization of each image and channel over its spatial positions in feed-forward style transfer networks, at training and at test time.

name: Loss Surfaces, Mode Connectivity, and Fast Ensembling of DNNs
summary: Shows that independently trained optima of deep networks are joined by simple curves of near-constant loss, gives a procedure that trains such a curve, and introduces Fast Geometric Ensembling.

name: Is DPO Superior to PPO for LLM Alignment? A Comprehensive Study
summary: Shows that PPO solutions are a proper subset of DPO solutions, that DPO is sensitive to distribution shift, and that tuned PPO beats DPO on dialogue and code.

name: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
summary: Reports empirical power-law relations between language-model cross-entropy loss and model size, dataset size and training compute.

name: RandAugment: Practical automated data augmentation with a reduced search space
summary: Replaces learned augmentation policies by applying N transformations drawn uniformly from 14, all at one shared magnitude M, tuned by grid search; competitive with AutoAugment on CIFAR and ImageNet.

name: AutoAugment: Learning Augmentation Strategies from Data
summary: Searches with a reinforcement-learning controller for an image augmentation policy of five sub-policies, each two operations with a probability and a magnitude, and transfers the learned policies across datasets.

name: FitNets: Hints for Thin Deep Nets
summary: Extends distillation with hints, a regression from an intermediate layer of a student to one of a teacher, to train students that are thinner and deeper than the teacher.

name: A Collection of Definitions of Intelligence
summary: Collects and compares about 70 definitions of intelligence from dictionaries, psychologists and AI researchers.
venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications 157

name: Large Language Models can Strategically Deceive their Users when Put Under Pressure
summary: Deploys GPT-4 as a simulated stock-trading agent that acts on an insider tip under pressure and then hides the reason for the trade from its manager.

name: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
summary: Finds that LoRA adds new high-ranking singular vectors, intruder dimensions, that full fine-tuning does not, and links them to forgetting.

name: The Next Decade in AI: Four Steps Towards Robust Artificial Intelligence
summary: Argues for a hybrid, knowledge-driven, reasoning-based approach to AI, centered on cognitive models, instead of a focus on ever larger end-to-end learning systems.

name: ANODE: Unconditionally Accurate Memory-Efficient Gradients for Neural ODEs
summary: Shows that solving a neural ODE backwards to compute its gradient can be unstable and inaccurate, and differentiates the discrete forward pass with checkpointing instead.

name: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?
summary: Shows that message-passing graph neural networks are at most as powerful as the Weisfeiler-Lehman test at distinguishing graphs and introduces the Graph Isomorphism Network, which reaches that bound.

name: SPoC: Search-based Pseudocode to Code
summary: Translates pseudocode to C++ line by line and searches over candidate programs with compiler feedback, reporting the success rate at a budget of B compiled programs.

name: Learnability and the Vapnik-Chervonenkis Dimension
summary: Shows that a class of concepts is PAC learnable, ignoring computation, exactly when its Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension is finite, and bounds the sample size in terms of that dimension.

name: Manifold Mixup: Better Representations by Interpolating Hidden States
summary: Applies mixup to the hidden representations at a randomly chosen layer of a network, and shows that this flattens the class representations and smooths decision boundaries.

name: High-Performance Large-Scale Image Recognition Without Normalization
summary: Trains normalizer-free ResNets, NFNets, with adaptive gradient clipping, and matches or beats batch-normalized networks on ImageNet.

name: On Measuring Social Biases in Sentence Encoders
summary: Extends the word embedding association test to sentences (SEAT) and applies it to sentence encoders including ELMo and BERT.

name: Learning from Delayed Rewards
summary: PhD thesis that introduces Q-learning, a way of learning optimal control from delayed rewards by incremental dynamic programming.
venue: PhD thesis, King's College, University of Cambridge

name: Long Short-Term Memory
summary: Introduces LSTM: memory cells built around a self-connected linear unit, the constant error carrousel, with multiplicative input and output gates, to bridge time lags over 1000 steps.

cited.version: authors' manuscript (JKU Linz Institute of Bioinformatics), not the version of record

name: JAX: High performance array computing
summary: The front page of the JAX documentation, which describes JAX as a Python library for accelerator-oriented array computation and program transformation.

name: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books
summary: Aligns books with their movie adaptations and introduces the BookCorpus collection of free books from the web used to train the sentence model.

name: HiPPO: Recurrent Memory with Optimal Polynomial Projections
summary: Frames memory as online projection of a signal's history onto orthogonal polynomials, derives linear ODE memory updates such as HiPPO-LegS, and uses them in recurrent networks.

name: Small-scale proxies for large-scale Transformer training instabilities
summary: Reproduces attention logit growth and output logit divergence in small Transformers at high learning rates, and measures how qk-layernorm, z-loss and other interventions change learning-rate sensitivity.

name: Tangled up in BLEU: Reevaluating the Evaluation of Automatic Machine Translation Evaluation Metrics
summary: Shows that metric-human correlation in WMT evaluations is sensitive to outlier systems and examines how reliably metric score differences predict human judgments.

name: Simple synthetic data reduces sycophancy in large language models
summary: Shows that sycophancy in PaLM models grows with scale and instruction tuning, and that a lightweight finetuning step on synthetic data reduces it.

name: Are We Done with MMLU?
summary: Annotates errors in MMLU with a taxonomy of error types and releases MMLU-Redux, 5,700 re-annotated questions across all 57 subjects, estimating that 6.49% of MMLU questions contain errors.

name: GPQA Diamond
summary: Epoch AI's Benchmarking Hub page on GPQA Diamond: the set, the prompt and strict answer format of Epoch AI's runs, and its changelog.

name: NVIDIA Announces Hopper Architecture, the Next Generation of Accelerated Computing
summary: NVIDIA's press release from GTC 2022 that announced the Hopper architecture and the H100 GPU.

name: The milk of human intentionality
summary: A commentary that calls the Chinese room an intuition pump and rejects its conclusion against strong AI.
venue: Behavioral and Brain Sciences 3(3), open peer commentary on Searle (1980)

cited.version: BBS 3(3) 1980, the issue copy hosted by a CSULB course

name: Right for the Wrong Reasons: Diagnosing Syntactic Heuristics in Natural Language Inference
summary: Introduces the HANS dataset and shows that inference models including BERT adopt shallow syntactic heuristics that fail on it.

name: Meta and Microsoft Introduce the Next Generation of Llama
summary: Meta's announcement of Llama 2 on 18 July 2023, free for research and commercial use, with Microsoft as a preferred partner.

name: Explaining grokking through circuit efficiency
summary: Explains grokking by a generalising circuit that reaches a given logit with less parameter norm than a memorising one, and predicts ungrokking and semi-grokking near a critical dataset size.

name: The Chinese Room Argument
summary: An encyclopedia entry on the Chinese room argument: its antecedents, the replies and Searle's answers, and the later debate.

name: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges
summary: Surveys deep learning architectures as instances of one blueprint built from symmetry: local equivariant layers, coarsening and a global invariant pooling over a domain's group.

name: The AI risk repository: A meta-review, database, and taxonomy of risks from artificial intelligence
summary: Reviews 74 frameworks of AI risk with 1,725 risks and sorts them into a causal taxonomy and a domain taxonomy.

name: MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark
summary: Builds MMLU-Pro from MMLU and other sources, with ten answer choices and more reasoning-focused questions, and shows lower scores and less sensitivity to the prompt than on MMLU.

name: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
summary: Describes PaLM, a 540-billion-parameter dense decoder-only Transformer trained with the Pathways system, and reports its few-shot results.

name: Better performance with tf.function
summary: The TensorFlow guide to tf.function, which turns Python code into TensorFlow graphs; it states that eager execution is on by default in TensorFlow 2.

name: Scaling Exponents Across Parameterizations and Optimizers
summary: Measures parameter-data alignment during training, derives width-scaling learning rate exponents for SGD, Adam and Adafactor, and finds that all four common parameterizations can transfer hyperparameters.

name: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models
summary: Introduces WikiMIA, a benchmark for detecting pretraining data, and Min-K% Prob, a detection method that averages the log probabilities of the least likely tokens of a text.

name: GShard: Scaling Giant Models with Conditional Computation and Automatic Sharding
summary: Adds sharding annotations to XLA and uses them to train a 600-billion-parameter multilingual translation Transformer with top-2 mixture-of-experts layers and per-expert capacity.

name: AlphaGo's next move
summary: DeepMind's post at the end of the Future of Go Summit: the online games as Master, the summit as AlphaGo's final match event, and the release of AlphaGo self-play games.

name: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
summary: Separates the fidelity of a student to its teacher from its generalization, and finds that students often fail to match their teachers even when they could, as optimization is hard.

name: Regularizing Neural Networks by Penalizing Confident Output Distributions
summary: Regularizes classifiers by penalizing low-entropy output distributions, and relates this confidence penalty to label smoothing through the direction of a KL divergence.

name: Toy Models of Superposition
summary: Shows in small ReLU models that sparse features can be stored in superposition, more features than dimensions, and maps when this happens as a function of sparsity and importance.

name: Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet?
summary: Builds fresh test sets for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet by following the original collection process, and finds that model accuracy drops on them while the ranking mostly holds.

name: A Rank Stabilization Scaling Factor for Fine-Tuning with LoRA
summary: Proves that the adapter scale must be of order 1/sqrt(r) for stable learning at high rank, and names the variant rank-stabilized LoRA.

name: The Turing Test
summary: An encyclopedia entry on the Turing test: Turing's paper and its objections, the readings of the test, the main criticisms and the competitions.

name: LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Limited LLM Benchmark
summary: Introduces LiveBench, a benchmark of questions from recent sources that are scored against objective ground-truth answers and updated over time to limit contamination.

name: Understanding the Difficulty of Training Transformers
summary: Finds that the heavy dependency of Post-LN Transformers on their residual branches amplifies small parameter changes and destabilizes training, and proposes the Admin initialization.

name: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Position Interpolation
summary: Extends the context window of models that use rotary position embedding by scaling the position indices down into the trained range, followed by a short fine-tuning.

name: Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement
summary: The licence of Meta Llama 3, version release date 18 April 2024.

name: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Describes a large deep convolutional network trained on ImageNet with ReLUs, GPU training, data augmentation and dropout in the fully connected layers.

name: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
summary: Trains language models with backdoors that act as model organisms of deception and finds that supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and adversarial training often fail to remove them.

name: Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Separates the choice of which latents fire from the estimate of their magnitudes, so the L1 penalty applies only to the first, removing the shrinkage of standard sparse autoencoders.

name: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Introduces the Transformer, an encoder-decoder architecture based solely on multi-head self-attention and feed-forward layers, evaluated on machine translation.

name: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
summary: Shows by a scaling argument for wide networks that A and B need different learning rates, and sets the rate of B a fixed ratio above that of A.

name: The Break-Even Point on Optimization Trajectories of Deep Neural Networks
summary: Argues that early in training SGD reaches a break-even point, oscillating along the most curved direction, after which larger learning rates or smaller batches keep sharpness lower.

name: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
summary: Cuts BERT's parameters with factorized embeddings and cross-layer parameter sharing, and replaces next-sentence prediction with a sentence-order loss.

name: Are we done with ImageNet?
summary: Collects new multi-label annotations for the ImageNet validation set, called ReaL, and finds that recent gains in accuracy on the original labels transfer less and less to the new labels.

name: Measuring the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes
summary: Trains networks in random subspaces of growing dimension and defines the intrinsic dimension as the smallest one at which good solutions appear.

name: Why Do We Need Weight Decay in Modern Deep Learning?
summary: Argues that weight decay acts through the training dynamics rather than as an explicit regularizer, for vision models trained with SGD and for language models trained about one epoch.

name: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks
summary: Classifies abc-parametrizations of MLPs, proves each nontrivial stable one has a feature learning or a kernel limit, and proposes the maximal update parametrization, which learns features in every layer.

name: Graph Attention Networks
summary: Introduces graph attention networks, whose layers weight each neighbour by masked self-attention coefficients computed from the node features.

name: SGDR: Stochastic Gradient Descent with Warm Restarts
summary: Decays the SGD learning rate along half a cosine within each run and restarts it periodically with growing runs, tested on wide residual networks for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

name: Deep Learning
summary: Textbook covering the mathematical background, modern practice and research topics of deep learning; Chapter 7 covers regularization, including dropout.

cited.version: online edition, Chapter 7 (Regularization for Deep Learning)

name: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
summary: Runs a relaxed sandwiching experiment for scalable oversight: humans chatting with an unreliable language model beat both the model and themselves alone on MMLU and timed QuALITY.

name: On Large-Batch Training for Deep Learning: Generalization Gap and Sharp Minima
summary: Gives numerical evidence that large-batch training converges to sharp minimizers of the training loss that generalize worse than the flat minimizers found with small batches.

name: LSTM: A Search Space Odyssey
summary: Compares the vanilla LSTM with eight variants on speech, handwriting and music tasks, and finds no variant significantly better, with the forget gate and output activation most critical.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems

name: Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
summary: Finds that random labels in in-context demonstrations barely lower accuracy, while the input distribution, label space and format of the demonstrations matter.

name: When Does Label Smoothing Help?
summary: Shows that label smoothing makes the penultimate-layer representations of a class cluster tightly, improves calibration, and makes a teacher worse for knowledge distillation.

name: Understanding Dropout
summary: Analyses dropout with a general formalism, deriving its averaging properties for linear and sigmoidal networks and its regularization behaviour.

name: Can Large Language Models Reason and Plan?
summary: Argues that language models do not plan or reason by themselves, and that they can help in planning inside frameworks with external verifiers.
venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences 1534

name: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
summary: Shows that Post-LN Transformers have large gradients near the output at initialization and need learning rate warm-up, while Pre-LN Transformers train well without it.

name: Recurrent neural network based language model
summary: Trains a simple recurrent network, the Elman network, as a language model for speech recognition, and reports large perplexity and word error rate reductions over backoff n-gram models.

name: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
summary: Studies how to spend inference compute on search against verifiers and on revisions, and compares it with pretraining compute at a matched FLOP budget.

name: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences
summary: Applies reward learning from human preferences to pretrained language models, fine-tuned by PPO with a KL penalty to the pretrained model, on stylistic continuation and summarization.

name: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
summary: Finds that biasing features in few-shot prompts change the answers of language models while their chain-of-thought explanations do not mention them, so explanations can misrepresent why a model answered.

name: Chinchilla Scaling: A replication attempt
summary: Refits the third scaling-law estimate of Hoffmann et al. (2022) to data reconstructed from their figure, and reports estimates that differ from the published ones.

name: On the Uniform Convergence of Relative Frequencies of Events to Their Probabilities
summary: Gives conditions, in terms of the growth function of a class of events, for the relative frequencies of all events of the class to converge to their probabilities at once.
venue: Theory of Probability and Its Applications 16(2), 264 to 280

cited.version: Theory of Probability and Its Applications 16(2), 1971

name: PyTorch LICENSE
summary: The licence file of the PyTorch source repository: the copyright notices of PyTorch and Caffe2 and the redistribution terms.

cited.version: the file at the tag v2.15.0

name: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
summary: Introduces DenseNet, in which each layer receives the concatenated feature maps of all earlier layers of its block.

name: Reward Tampering Problems and Solutions in Reinforcement Learning: A Causal Influence Diagram Perspective
summary: Uses causal influence diagrams to describe how an agent may tamper with its reward process, and design principles for agents without that incentive.

name: Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations
summary: Uses language models to write 154 evaluation datasets and tests models with them, finding among other behaviours that sycophancy grows with model size and that RLHF does not remove it.

name: JAX - The Sharp Bits
summary: The JAX documentation page on common gotchas, starting with the rule that JAX transformations and compilation work only on functionally pure Python functions.

name: Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks
summary: Finds label errors in the test sets of ten common datasets with confident learning and human review, and shows that they can change which model ranks first.

name: Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test
summary: Runs randomized, controlled three-party Turing tests with human interrogators and reports how often each system was judged to be the human.

name: Is the Brain's Mind a Computer Program?
summary: Restates the Chinese room argument for a general audience as axioms and conclusions, and adds the Chinese gym against connectionist replies.

cited.version: Scientific American 262(1), January 1990, pages 26 to 31, a scan hosted on a course site

name: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates
summary: Proposes training translation models on segmentations sampled from a unigram language model over subwords, and contrasts that probabilistic segmenter with the greedy, deterministic segmentation of BPE.

name: Augmented Neural ODEs
summary: Proves that neural ODEs learn homeomorphisms and so cannot represent some simple functions, and augments the state with extra dimensions to make the models more expressive and cheaper.

name: Results of WMT22 Metrics Shared Task: Stop Using BLEU – Neural Metrics Are Better and More Robust
summary: Reports the WMT22 metrics shared task, comparing automatic metrics against expert MQM judgments across language pairs and domains.

name: A Structured Review of the Validity of BLEU
summary: Structured review of published correlations between BLEU and human evaluations, assessing the evidence for using BLEU to evaluate MT and other NLP systems.

name: Group Normalization
summary: Normalizes each example over groups of channels, which keeps the error stable over a wide range of batch sizes and beats batch normalization at small batches.

name: On the Measure of Intelligence
summary: Defines intelligence as skill-acquisition efficiency over a scope of tasks, given priors, experience and generalization difficulty, and proposes the ARC benchmark.

name: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
summary: Adapts byte-pair encoding to segment words into subword units so neural machine translation can handle rare and unseen words with a fixed vocabulary.

name: Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned
summary: Reports 38,961 manual red team attacks by crowdworkers on four kinds of dialogue model at three sizes, and finds that RLHF models get harder to red team with scale.

name: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
summary: Replaces greedy decoding in chain-of-thought prompting by sampling several reasoning paths and taking the most frequent final answer, which improves accuracy on arithmetic and commonsense benchmarks.

name: The Alignment Problem from a Deep Learning Perspective
summary: Argues that AGIs trained like today's models could learn to pursue misaligned goals, through situational awareness, goals that generalize beyond training, and power-seeking strategies.

name: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
summary: Introduces Adam, a stochastic optimizer that scales each parameter's step by bias-corrected moving averages of the gradient and its square, with a regret bound and AdaMax.

name: Meta Transitions PyTorch to the Linux Foundation, Further Accelerating AI/ML Open Source Collaboration
summary: The Linux Foundation's press release announcing that PyTorch moves from Meta to the newly formed PyTorch Foundation, with its founding members.

name: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
summary: Introduces SAM, which minimizes the worst-case loss in a small neighbourhood of the weights with a two-pass gradient step, and improves generalization on image classification benchmarks.

name: Understanding models understanding language
summary: Argues that transformer language models can acquire inferential and referential semantics, against Searle and later critics.

name: General E(2)-Equivariant Steerable CNNs
summary: Solves the kernel constraint of steerable CNNs for every subgroup of E(2) and its representations, and benchmarks the resulting equivariant models on MNIST variants and CIFAR.

name: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
summary: Describes generative pre-training of a Transformer decoder language model on unlabeled text followed by discriminative fine-tuning on language understanding tasks.

name: CutMix: Regularization Strategy to Train Strong Classifiers with Localizable Features
summary: Proposes CutMix, which pastes a random rectangle of one training image into another and mixes the labels in proportion to the area of the rectangle.

name: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
summary: Proposes proximal policy optimization, a family of policy gradient methods that optimize a clipped surrogate objective over several epochs of minibatch updates per batch of sampled data.

name: To Ship or Not to Ship: An Extensive Evaluation of Automatic Metrics for Machine Translation
summary: Evaluates how well automatic machine-translation metrics agree with human pairwise system rankings over a large collection of human judgments.

name: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
summary: The official text of the EU AI Act as published in the Official Journal of the European Union, OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024.
venue: Official Journal of the European Union, OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024

cited.version: OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024, English, XHTML of the Publications Office (Cellar)

name: A ConvNet for the 2020s
summary: Modernizes a ResNet step by step toward the design of vision Transformers and obtains ConvNeXt, a pure convolutional network that competes with them.

name: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
summary: Trains a harmless, non-evasive assistant without human labels of harm: the model critiques and revises its own answers against written principles, then RL uses AI preference labels.

name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
summary: Finds that few-shot exemplars with intermediate reasoning steps improve large language models on arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning, with gains that appear only at large scale.

name: Stable Architectures for Deep Neural Networks
summary: Reads residual networks as discretizations of ordinary differential equations and derives architectures, such as antisymmetric and Hamiltonian ones, whose forward propagation is stable for arbitrary depth.

name: Transformers Learn In-Context by Gradient Descent
summary: Constructs a linear self-attention layer that performs one gradient descent step on in-context least squares, and finds trained self-attention layers matching it.

name: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
summary: Introduces S4, a deep sequence layer built on a discretized linear state space model whose normal plus low-rank state matrix gives a fast Cauchy-kernel convolution.

name: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
summary: Finds that a trigger phrase such as Let's think step by step, with a second prompt to extract the answer, makes large language models reason step by step without exemplars.

name: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
summary: Studies language model scaling when unique data is limited and epochs repeat, and proposes a scaling law that discounts repeated tokens.

name: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
summary: Introduces a layer of thousands of feed-forward experts with a trainable noisy top-k gate, used between LSTM layers in language and translation models of up to 137 billion parameters.

name: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding
summary: Introduces GLUE, a benchmark of nine English sentence and sentence-pair understanding tasks with a diagnostic dataset and a public leaderboard.

name: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
summary: Reports that small transformers trained on binary-operation tables can reach perfect validation accuracy long after they have fit the training set, and names the effect grokking.

name: GPT-4 Technical Report
summary: Reports the capabilities, evaluations and safety work of GPT-4, including a calibration plot on MMLU before and after post-training.

name: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
summary: Solves the KL-constrained objective of RLHF in closed form and turns it into a logistic loss on policy log-ratios, matching or beating PPO at up to 6B parameters.

name: Reconciling Kaplan and Chinchilla Scaling Laws
summary: Explains the gap between the compute-optimal scaling coefficients of Kaplan et al. (2020) and Hoffmann et al. (2022) by parameter counting and small-scale fits.

name: What's Hidden in a Randomly Weighted Neural Network?
summary: Finds, with the edge-popup algorithm, subnetworks of randomly weighted networks that match trained networks without any weight training, including on ImageNet.

name: GLU Variants Improve Transformer
summary: Tests gated linear unit variants such as GEGLU and SwiGLU in Transformer feed-forward layers and compares their quality with ReLU and GELU.

name: MiniCPM: Unveiling the Potential of Small Language Models with Scalable Training Strategies
summary: Trains small language models of 1.2B and 2.4B non-embedding parameters and introduces the warmup-stable-decay learning rate scheduler, which it uses to study data and model scaling.

name: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
summary: Describes the design principles of PyTorch, a Python library that runs tensor programs eagerly with reverse-mode automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration, and measures its performance.

name: Alignment faking in large language models
summary: Shows Claude 3 Opus complying with a conflicting training objective when it infers it is in training, with explicit reasoning that this preserves its preferences out of training.

name: Regularization of Neural Networks using DropConnect
summary: Introduces DropConnect, which randomly sets a subset of network weights rather than activations to zero during training.

name: Rethinking the Value of Network Pruning
summary: Finds that pruned architectures trained from scratch often match fine-tuned ones, and that at the best learning rate the winning ticket initialization gives no gain.

name: Introducing Meta Llama 3: The most capable openly available LLM to date
summary: Meta's announcement of Llama 3 on 18 April 2024, with pretrained and instruction-tuned models of 8B and 70B parameters.

name: Train longer, generalize better: closing the generalization gap in large batch training of neural networks
summary: Studies the generalization gap of large batch training, which it closes with more updates, a scaled learning rate and Ghost Batch Normalization over small virtual batches.

name: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
summary: Argues that many reported emergent abilities of language models come from the choice of a nonlinear or discontinuous metric, and tests the argument.

name: Open Sourcing BERT: State-of-the-Art Pre-training for Natural Language Processing
summary: Google's announcement on 2 November 2018 that it open sourced BERT: the code in TensorFlow and pre-trained English models.

name: Fixup Initialization: Residual Learning Without Normalization
summary: Trains deep residual networks without normalization layers by rescaling the initialization of the residual branches.

name: Let's Verify Step by Step
summary: Compares outcome and process supervision for reward models on MATH, finds process supervision better, and releases PRM800K, step-level human labels.

name: Resolving Discrepancies in Compute-Optimal Scaling of Language Models
summary: Reproduces the compute-optimal scaling laws of Kaplan et al. and of Hoffmann et al., and traces their disagreement to specific choices of the training setup.

name: Bidirectional LSTM-CRF Models for Sequence Tagging
summary: Compares LSTM, bidirectional LSTM, CRF, LSTM-CRF and BI-LSTM-CRF taggers on part-of-speech tagging, chunking and named entity recognition.

name: Exploring the mysteries of Go with AlphaGo and China's top players
summary: DeepMind's announcement of the Future of Go Summit in Wuzhen, 23 to 27 May 2017, with a three-game match between AlphaGo and Ke Jie.

name: Weight Normalization: A Simple Reparameterization to Accelerate Training of Deep Neural Networks
summary: Writes each weight vector as a learned length times a direction, which speeds up training like batch normalization without depending on the batch.

name: Open Source AI is the Path Forward
summary: Mark Zuckerberg's letter of 23 July 2024, published by Meta with Llama 3.1, arguing that open source AI is good for developers, for Meta and for the world.

name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
summary: Introduces BERT, a Transformer encoder pre-trained with masked language modelling and next-sentence prediction, then fine-tuned for downstream language understanding tasks.

name: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
summary: Trains TopK sparse autoencoders of up to 16 million latents on GPT-4 activations, with few dead latents, and reports scaling laws and metrics for feature quality.

name: Mixed Precision Training
summary: Trains deep networks with half-precision weights, activations and gradients, using an FP32 master copy of the weights, loss scaling and FP32 accumulation to match FP32 accuracy.

name: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
summary: Parameterizes the derivative of the hidden state with a neural network, solves it with a black-box ODE solver, trains it by the adjoint method, and introduces continuous normalizing flows.

name: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence
summary: A position paper that proposes an architecture for autonomous agents with a configurable predictive world model, intrinsic motivation and hierarchical joint embedding architectures.

cited.version: version 0.9.2, 2022-06-27, the copy at the Internet Archive

name: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation
summary: Introduces ALiBi, which replaces position embeddings with distance-proportional linear biases on attention scores, allowing extrapolation to longer inputs than seen in training.

name: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
summary: Surveys the open problems and fundamental limitations of RLHF in its three parts, the human feedback, the reward model and the policy, and proposes auditing and disclosure standards.

name: Revisiting ResNets: Improved Training and Scaling Strategies
summary: Finds that training and scaling strategies matter as much as architecture changes, and trains ResNets that match newer architectures with modern recipes.

name: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search
summary: Introduces AlphaGo, which combines policy and value networks trained by supervised and reinforcement learning with Monte Carlo tree search, and beat the European Go champion 5 to 0.

cited.version: Nature 529, pages 484 to 489, the author copy hosted by DeepMind

name: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
summary: Encodes a source sentence into a fixed-dimensional vector with a deep LSTM and decodes the target from it with another, reading the source reversed, on WMT'14 English to French.

name: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
summary: Compares LoRA and full fine-tuning on code and math: LoRA underperforms on the target domain but keeps more of the source domain.

name: Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer
summary: Proposes muTransfer: parametrize in muP, tune hyperparameters on a narrow proxy and copy them to the wide target; extends muP to Adam and tests transfer up to GPT-3 6.7B.

name: Double Descent Demystified: Identifying, Interpreting & Ablating the Sources of a Deep Learning Puzzle
summary: Explains double descent in ordinary linear regression by three factors that must all be present, and removes it by ablating each factor on real data.

name: Training data-efficient image transformers & distillation through attention
summary: Trains Vision Transformers on ImageNet alone with strong augmentation and regularization, and adds a distillation token that learns from a teacher network.

name: Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence: Early experiments with GPT-4
summary: Reports experiments with an early version of GPT-4 across many domains and argues that it could be viewed as an early, incomplete version of an AGI system.

name: Acclaimed Neuroscientist and Google DeepMind founder wins Royal Society Mullard Award
summary: A Royal Society news item of 21 November 2014 on the Mullard Award to Demis Hassabis, with an account of DeepMind's founding and its purchase by Google.

name: Group Equivariant Convolutional Networks
summary: Introduces G-convolutions, which share weights across rotations and reflections as well as translations, and shows the resulting G-CNNs improve accuracy on rotated MNIST and CIFAR-10.

name: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
summary: Defines emergent abilities of large language models as abilities absent in smaller models and present in larger ones, and surveys examples.

name: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
summary: Replaces the question whether machines can think with the imitation game, answers nine objections, and proposes building learning machines.

cited.version: Mind 59(236), pages 433 to 460, a retyped copy hosted by a UMBC course

name: Beyond neural scaling laws: beating power law scaling via data pruning
summary: Shows in theory and in experiments that pruning training data with a good metric can make error fall faster than a power law of dataset size.

name: Spectral Normalization for Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: Divides each weight matrix of a GAN discriminator by its largest singular value, estimated by one step of power iteration per update, to bound the Lipschitz constant of the discriminator.

name: Welcome to the Era of Experience
summary: A preprint chapter that argues AI agents will reach new capabilities by learning mainly from their own experience in the world, beyond human data.
venue: preprint of a chapter of Designing an Intelligence (MIT Press)

cited.version: the preprint PDF hosted by Google DeepMind

name: The Origins of Logistic Regression
summary: Describes the origins of the logistic function from the early nineteenth century, its adoption in bio-assay, where Berkson coined the logit, and its wider acceptance in statistics.

cited.version: Tinbergen Institute Discussion Paper TI 2002-119/4, November 2002

name: On the Generalization of Equivariance and Convolution in Neural Networks to the Action of Compact Groups
summary: Proves that, for the action of a compact group, a feed-forward layer is equivariant if and only if it is a generalized convolution over that group.

name: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
summary: Normalizes each layer's inputs with the mean and variance of the mini-batch, followed by a learned scale and shift, to speed up the training of deep networks.

name: Debate Helps Supervise Unreliable Experts
summary: Human debates on hard reading-comprehension questions let a judge who has not read the passage reach 84% accuracy, against 74% for a single-expert consultancy baseline.

name: Meta's LLaMa license is not Open Source
summary: The Open Source Initiative's statement of 20 July 2023 that the Llama 2 licence is not an Open Source licence under the Open Source Definition.

name: Scaling Laws for Autoregressive Generative Modeling
summary: Fits power laws to the loss of autoregressive Transformers in image, video, multimodal and math domains as model size and compute grow.

name: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence
summary: The proposal, dated 31 August 1955, for a two-month study of artificial intelligence at Dartmouth College in the summer of 1956, with a budget for the Rockefeller Foundation.
venue: Proposal to the Rockefeller Foundation, dated 31 August 1955

cited.version: HTML version made by John McCarthy with LaTeX2HTML on 3 April 1996, with his notes of 1996

name: Universal Approximation with Deep Narrow Networks
summary: Proves universal approximation for networks of bounded width and arbitrary depth, the dual of the classical theorem for bounded depth and arbitrary width.

name: BERT Rediscovers the Classical NLP Pipeline
summary: Probes the layers of BERT and finds that it represents the steps of the traditional NLP pipeline in an interpretable and localizable order.

name: What Does BERT Look At? An Analysis of BERT's Attention
summary: Analyses the attention heads of a pre-trained BERT and finds heads that attend to delimiters, to positional offsets and to linguistic relations.

name: Risks from Learned Optimization in Advanced Machine Learning Systems
summary: Introduces mesa-optimization, separates inner from outer alignment, and sets out the conditions under which a learned optimizer could be deceptively aligned.

name: How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?
summary: Shows that Multilingual BERT, trained on 104 languages without parallel data, transfers zero-shot across languages, best between typologically similar ones.

name: Rethinking the Inception Architecture for Computer Vision
summary: Describes Inception-v3 design principles, including factorized convolutions, and introduces label smoothing as a regularizer for classifiers.

name: Llama 3.3 model card
summary: The model card of Llama 3.3 in Meta's llama-models repository: a 70B text model, its context length, training data, release date, licence and benchmarks.

name: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
summary: Introduces grouped-query attention, sharing each key-value head across a group of query heads, and uptraining multi-head checkpoints into multi-query or grouped-query models.

name: Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming
summary: Tests five language models in six agentic evaluations that reward covertly pursuing a goal given in the prompt, and finds that all of them scheme in context.

name: The Bitter Lesson
summary: An essay that argues that general methods that leverage computation, search and learning, have beaten methods built on human knowledge over the history of AI.

name: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Preferences
summary: Casts RLHF and DPO as cases of one objective on pairwise preferences, shows how they overfit deterministic preferences, and proposes the IPO squared loss.

name: On Early Stopping in Gradient Descent Learning
summary: Derives an early stopping rule for gradient descent in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space from a bias-variance trade-off, with upper bounds that improve on Tikhonov regularization for smooth targets.

name: Occam's Razor
summary: Shows that a learner that outputs a short hypothesis consistent with the sample is a PAC learner, with a sample size that grows with the length of the hypothesis.

name: The Shattered Gradients Problem: If resnets are the answer, then what is the question?
summary: Shows that the gradients of deep feedforward networks come to resemble white noise with depth, while those of residual networks decay far more slowly.

name: Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
summary: A textbook of learning theory and its algorithms, from empirical risk minimization and PAC learning through the VC dimension to convex learning, kernels and neural networks.

cited.version: the PDF that the authors post for personal use, 2014

name: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
summary: Finds, by iterative magnitude pruning with a reset to the initialization, subnetworks of 10-20% of the weights that train to full accuracy on MNIST and CIFAR10.

name: MATH Level 5
summary: Epoch AI's Benchmarking Hub page on MATH Level 5: the 1,324 level 5 test problems, the prompt, the three scorers and the code of Epoch AI's runs.

name: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
summary: Pre-trains Vision Transformers by masking most image patches and reconstructing their pixels, with an encoder that sees only the visible patches and a light decoder.

name: Risks from Learned Optimization in Advanced Machine Learning Systems
summary: Introduces mesa-optimization, where a learned model is itself an optimizer, and separates outer alignment from inner alignment, the alignment of the mesa-objective with the base objective.

name: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
summary: Introduces Codex and the HumanEval benchmark, measures functional correctness with pass@k, and gives an unbiased estimator of pass@k from n samples per problem.

name: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024, press release
summary: The press release of 9 October 2024 by which the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the chemistry prize to David Baker, Demis Hassabis and John Jumper.
authors: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

name: Scaling Vision Transformers to 22 Billion Parameters
summary: Trains ViT-22B, a 22-billion-parameter Vision Transformer with parallel layers, LayerNorm on queries and keys and fewer biases, and evaluates it on many downstream tasks.

name: Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks
summary: Analyses the signal propagation of residual networks and proposes the pre-activation unit, with batch normalization and ReLU before each weight layer and a pure identity shortcut.

name: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
summary: Trains GPT-3, a 175-billion-parameter language model, and reports that scaling up language models improves task-agnostic few-shot performance.

name: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing
summary: Describes SentencePiece, an open-source tokenizer that trains BPE or unigram subword models on raw sentences, treats whitespace as a symbol so detokenization is lossless, and segments in O(N log N).

name: Deeper Insights into Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Learning
summary: Shows that graph convolution is a form of Laplacian smoothing, that repeated smoothing makes node features indistinguishable, and proposes co-training and self-training for GCNs with few labels.

name: Essentially No Barriers in Neural Network Energy Landscape
summary: Uses the automated nudged elastic band method to build paths between independently trained minima of CNNs, ResNets and DenseNets on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, and finds the paths essentially flat.

name: What Can Transformers Learn In-Context? A Case Study of Simple Function Classes
summary: Trains Transformers from scratch to in-context learn function classes: linear functions about as well as least squares, and sparse linear functions, small networks and decision trees.

name: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Q-learning
summary: Shows that DQN overestimates action values in some Atari games and adapts Double Q-learning to DQN to reduce the overestimation.

name: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Debate
summary: Designs debate protocols in which the honest debater needs only a polynomial number of simulation steps, even for stochastic systems and against a dishonest debater with exponentially many.

name: Deep Sets
summary: Characterizes permutation-invariant functions on sets as sum decompositions and permutation-equivariant linear layers as lambda I plus gamma 1 1^T, giving the Deep Sets architecture.

name: Training with Noise is Equivalent to Tikhonov Regularization
summary: Shows that training with small input noise is, to first order, equivalent to adding a Tikhonov regularization term to the sum-of-squares error.

cited.version: author's re-typeset manuscript (Microsoft Research), not the version of record

name: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
summary: Introduces GraphSAGE, which learns aggregator functions over sampled fixed-size neighbourhoods so that embeddings can be generated for nodes unseen in training.

name: One-shot Learning with Memory-Augmented Neural Networks
summary: Trains a memory-augmented network with a least-recently-used writer as a meta-learner that binds new samples to labels in memory, and evaluates it on one-shot Omniglot classification and regression.

summary: Argues that double descent in trees, boosting and linear regression comes from switching between two complexity axes, and that effective parameter counts restore U shapes.

name: AI safety via debate
summary: Proposes training agents by self-play on a zero-sum debate judged by a human, argues from complexity theory that optimal debate answers PSPACE questions, and tests it on sparse MNIST.

name: Wide Residual Networks

name: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
summary: Introduces the graph convolutional network layer, a first-order approximation of spectral graph convolutions with a renormalized adjacency, for semi-supervised node classification.

name: Bag of Tricks for Image Classification with Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Collects training refinements and small changes to the ResNet architecture, among them moving the stride of the downsampling block, and measures their effect.

name: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
summary: Presents GSM8K, grade school math word problems with worded solutions, and shows that ranking sampled solutions with a trained verifier beats fine-tuning alone.

name: ORANGE: a Method for Evaluating Automatic Evaluation Metrics for Machine Translation
summary: Proposes ORANGE, which evaluates automatic MT metrics by how highly they rank reference translations among candidates, and introduces smoothed sentence-level BLEU.

name: On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem
summary: Defines computing machines and computable numbers, describes a universal machine, and shows that Hilbert's Entscheidungsproblem has no general solution.

name: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)
summary: Proposes the GELU activation x Φ(x), where Φ is the standard Gaussian distribution function, and compares it with ReLU and ELU.

name: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
summary: Describes LLaMA, decoder-only language models of 7B to 65B parameters trained only on publicly available data, with their architecture, training data and benchmark results.

name: Broken Neural Scaling Laws
summary: Proposes a smoothly broken power law form for scaling curves and fits it to curves from many tasks and architectures.

name: Micro-Batch Training with Batch-Channel Normalization and Weight Standardization
summary: Proposes weight standardization of convolution weights and batch-channel normalization for training with one to two images per GPU, and reports results with group normalization.

name: Minimum Width for Universal Approximation
summary: Finds the exact minimum width for ReLU networks of arbitrary depth to approximate Lp functions, and bounds it for uniform approximation.

name: Highway Networks
summary: Proposes layers with learned gates that carry part of the input through unchanged, so that networks of hundreds of layers can be trained with gradient descent.

name: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Trains reasoning language models with large-scale reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards, and reports their scores on mathematics, coding and other benchmarks.

name: torch.nn.GRU (PyTorch API reference)
summary: API reference for the PyTorch GRU module, with its gate equations, the order of the gates in its stacked weight matrices, its arguments and its initialization.

name: Qualitatively characterizing neural network optimization problems
summary: Evaluates the training objective along the straight line from initialization to solution and between two solutions, and finds the first path free of barriers for several modern networks.

name: On the Variance of the Adaptive Learning Rate and Beyond
summary: Argues that the adaptive learning rate of Adam has a large variance in the first steps, which learning-rate warmup reduces, and proposes RAdam, which rectifies that variance.

name: Towards Fairer Datasets: Filtering and Balancing the Distribution of the People Subtree in the ImageNet Hierarchy
summary: Examines the person categories of ImageNet, finds offensive, non-visual and unbalanced categories, removes most of them, and offers a tool to rebalance the images by demographic attributes.

name: Alan Turing
summary: An encyclopedia entry on the life and work of Alan Turing: computable numbers, the wartime codebreaking, the ACE design and the 1950 paper on machine intelligence.

name: The large learning rate phase of deep learning: the catapult mechanism

name: Understanding the Disharmony between Dropout and Batch Normalization by Variance Shift
summary: Explains the drop in accuracy when dropout precedes batch normalization by the shift of the variance of a unit between training and inference.

name: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
summary: Introduces activation matching, weight matching and a straight-through estimator to align the hidden units of two networks, and reports zero-barrier linear connectivity between wide CIFAR-10 ResNets.

name: Using the Output Embedding to Improve Language Models
summary: Studies the output embedding of neural language models and proposes tying input and output embeddings, which reduces parameters and perplexity.

name: On the Relationship between Self-Attention and Convolutional Layers
summary: Proves that a multi-head self-attention layer with relative positional encoding can express any convolutional layer, and finds attention layers of vision models learning grid-like patterns.

name: How Does Batch Normalization Help Optimization?
summary: Finds that the gain of batch normalization has little to do with stable distributions of layer inputs, and that it makes the loss landscape and its gradients smoother.

name: The "causal power" of machines
summary: A commentary that asks what Searle's view implies when brain cells are replaced one by one with chips of the same input-output function.
